info.name: Lesotho Health Sandbox
info.description:
Full API collection for the Lesotho health system sandbox (PROD: lesotho-bkm.xyz).
Services: BKM Mediator, OpenHIM, HAPI FHIR, DHIS2, OpenLMIS, Keycloak.

# Setup (do this first)

1. Import this collection. It is pre-configured for PROD via collection variables.
2. Open the collection -> Variables tab. Postman keeps two columns: Initial (from this
   file) and Current (what actually runs). Make sure the CURRENT value column matches:
   - keycloak    = https://lesotho-bkm.xyz/auth        (NOTE: /auth path, NO :8083 port)
   - hapi        = https://fhir.lesotho-bkm.xyz/fhir
   - mediator    = https://lesotho-bkm.xyz/mediator-api
   - lesothosite = https://lesotho-bkm.xyz/mediator-api
   - openhim_ch  = https://lesotho-bkm.xyz/mediator-api
   - openlmis    = https://lmis.lesotho-bkm.xyz
   - dhis2       = https://dhis2.lesotho-bkm.xyz
   - openhim_api = https://lesotho-bkm.xyz/openhim
   If any Current value still shows http://localhost:PORT, the fastest fix is to DELETE and
   RE-IMPORT the collection (a fresh import copies Initial -> Current).
3. Passwords are blank in the shared file. Set these Current values yourself:
   - kc_pass  = the bkm-admin password
   (and, per request, the DHIS2 / OpenHIM / OpenLMIS basic-auth passwords if you use them.)

# Get a Keycloak token

The web portal uses PKCE (browser), but the realm's public client opensrp-client has Direct
Access Grants enabled, so Postman uses the password grant.

1. Set the kc_pass variable (step 3 above).
2. Run: 9. Keycloak -> Token - bkm-admin password grant (opensrp-client). Click Send.
3. Expect 200 with an access_token. A test script saves it to {{token}} (open the Postman
   Console, Ctrl+Alt+C, to see 'token saved'). The collection-level Bearer uses {{token}},
   so folders 2 (Mediator), 3 (Mappings), 5 (HAPI FHIR) now work automatically.
4. The token lasts 5 minutes. On a 401, just re-Send the token request.

Endpoint: {{keycloak}}/realms/opensrp/protocol/openid-connect/token
Body (x-www-form-urlencoded): grant_type=password, client_id=opensrp-client,
username=bkm-admin, password={{kc_pass}}

# OpenLMIS token

Run: 8. OpenLMIS -> Auth - get token. It saves {{lmis_token}} for the other OpenLMIS requests.
HAPI FHIR and the mediator are open on prod (no token needed); the bearer is there for any
protected route.

# Troubleshooting

- SSL error WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER: the URL resolved to https on an http port (e.g.
  https://lesotho-bkm.xyz:8083). Fix the keycloak Current value to https://lesotho-bkm.xyz/auth
  (no port, /auth path).
- 401 invalid_grant: wrong password (kc_pass). 401 invalid_client: client_id got changed -
  set it back to opensrp-client.
- Corporate proxy can break TLS: Postman Settings -> Proxy -> turn off system/custom proxy.
- Self-signed services (OpenHIM): Settings -> General -> SSL certificate verification OFF.
- Some requests have relative URLs (no host) - prepend the right {{base}} variable.
- facility_id / program_id / orderable_id are old Maseru demo ids; prod is Mafeteng - fetch
  real ids via OpenLMIS -> Facilities/Orderables after getting the LMIS token.

item.name: 1. Mediator — FHIR Endpoints (via OpenHIM :5001)

request.description: Dispense medicine to a patient. Fans out: OpenLMIS DEBIT + DHIS2 data value.
Stock receipt (CREDIT) from facility to VHW. Fans out: OpenLMIS CREDIT.
App dispense form submission — same fan-out as MedicationDispense.
Stock order from the Order register. Buffered and batch-dispatched to OpenLMIS. Add ?immediate=true to dispatch immediately.
Stock adjustment. adjustmentReason must be: expired | damaged | lost_stolen
Creates a stock-issue Task on HAPI FHIR for the VHW to accept in the app.

item.description: Stock events the Android app posts through the OpenHIM channel. All reach the BKM mediator which fans out to OpenLMIS + DHIS2.

item.name: 2. Mediator — Admin APIs (:3000 direct)

request.description: Returns: order buffer, dispatch log, next dispatch time, schedule frequency, performers by org unit.
Shows buffered orders waiting for the next batch dispatch.
Dispatch the buffered orders to OpenLMIS. Set force:true to re-dispatch an already-dispatched period.
Clears the dispatch log so the current period can be re-dispatched.
frequency: daily | weekly | monthly
Triggers facility aggregation for the given period (YYYYMM). Omit period to use current month.
Returns all VHW/Practitioner mappings with village, region, facility, phone, email.
Creates FHIR Tasks on HAPI FHIR. The Android app picks them up on next sync.
Marks a Task as completed so it cannot be accepted again (BR-04).
Triggers the dhis2-integration service to push latest OpenLMIS stock data to DHIS2.
Returns all runtime config values (IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_MS, REJECT_DUPLICATE_DISPENSE, etc).
Returns a valid OpenLMIS Bearer token (mediator fetches it internally).

item.name: Bundle Sync — POST stock QRs from app bundle

request.description: Called by the fhir-proxy mirror on app sync-up bundles. Extracts stock QRs and fans them out.

item.description: Admin/management endpoints on the mediator. Requires port 3000 exposed (already added to docker-compose).

request.description: Returns live performer map and medication map.
Pulls all Practitioners from HAPI FHIR and adds any not yet in the performer map.
SNOMED 386452003 = Supply management. These are the stock commodity groups shown in the Inventory and Stock Order registers.
Preliminary observations = current stock on hand (SOH) per commodity.
The Composition lists all Binary config resource IDs the app downloads. If this gets corrupted the app loses all configs.
Check if OpenHIM core is up. Disable SSL verification (self-signed cert).
Fetches an OpenLMIS user token. Auto-saves to {{lmis_token}} collection variable.

query.description: Optional — omit to see all orderables

request.description: Direct stock DEBIT (Consumed/Dispensed reason). Usually done via mediator, not directly.
Get a JWT for the opensrp-admin user (the VHW / practitioner used in tests).
Returns the static PractitionerDetails bundle so the Android app can complete login.
